checks.name: expanded-profile-observed-batch-coverage
checks.reason: Read-only periodic observations captured 51 active Decode requests with no recorded preemptions. One observed point had one queued request. Endpoint teardown scrape failures are retained in the observation summary. These observations do not claim continuous coverage or a performance/SLA verdict.

checks.name: expanded-online-predictor-continuous-availability
checks.reason: Positive P/D decisions were observed in both load and recovery, but recovery also recorded ten model_not_ready decisions for Decode. Planner held the current replica count and endpoint floor. Continuous predictor availability is not certified; the specific cause is not isolated. Successful file bootstrap/restart and API requests do not remove this limitation.

checks.name: expanded-online-request-completeness
checks.reason: All recorded load/recovery API requests completed. Latency targets and empty visible text are separate from API completion; exact token quality and production SLA are not certified.

checks.name: narrow-decode-profile-fit
checks.reason: The complete max-num-seqs=16 sweep could not initialize native Decode regression, even without an SLA constraint. Preserve this failed profile. Fresh qualification uses a distinct max-num-seqs=64 identity and a complete new sweep, without mixing/selecting samples or overriding readiness.

checks.name: production-latency-sla
checks.reason: Bounded functionality is certified, not production latency. The original DeepSeek OSL512 case exceeded the client timeout; Qwen32 also exceeded the functional TTFT target. Fresh r3 C16 DeepSeek load completed 249 requests without API errors but TTFT p95 was 2596.74 ms against the 1000 ms target; one request had no visible text despite a complete token stream. Three recovery requests completed within targets. This is functional transport/scaling evidence, not text-quality or production SLA certification. All failures and the separately configured shorter-output run remain recorded.

checks.name: ascend-colocated-pd
checks.reason: The initial two-device/five-worker fixture failed because ADXL rejects connections to the same physical NPU. The qualified replacement uses five distinct NPUs; no engine or image change.

checks.name: hybrid-inflight-forced-failure
checks.reason: Hybrid tests cover block boundaries, concurrency, cancellation after first token and recovery. Mid-transfer process termination and hybrid resource soak are not covered by the standard-connector soak.

checks.name: ascend-gms-vmm-and-nixl-media
checks.reason: Previously deferred Ascend GMS/VMM shared allocations and NIXL media paths remain unqualified.

checks.name: model-backed-multimodal-omni-and-full-parallel-matrix
checks.reason: No suitable model-specific media assets in this campaign; media primitives are tested. Only recorded TP/DP/EP configurations are certified, without restricting native parameters.

checks.name: independent-extensions
checks.reason: DRA on the newer experimental cluster, G4 remote cache, independent Omni hidden-state channel, Kubernetes GMS/failover and hardware power writes remain outside this delivery scope.

notes: r3 uses installed packages; runtime tests mount only test drivers.

Fresh expanded DeepSeek r3 profile identity binds the r3 image, Hybrid transport and max-num-seqs=64. The original max-num-seqs=16 offline fit failed and is retained. Historical small/Qwen32 r1 profiles cannot be relabeled for r3 use.
No production SLA or untested parallelism certification. Whole-checkpoint SHA256 equivalence is scoped to the recorded Ascend DeepSeek model on the two tested nodes.
Historical r1 plain-connector assertion, r2 import abort and initial failed tool invocation are retained.
